headings.title: Parameter storage, acceptance and exact inputs

html:
Parameter storage, acceptance and exact inputs

Parameters and Database explains operator setup. This guide separates live saved records, accepted task inputs and consumer projections. Editing a saved ordinary parameter changes future acceptance; it does not replace the literal value already owned by a queued or running task.

flowchart TD E[Explicit create or edit] --> V[Typed validation and canonical identity] V --> S[Live Parameter Store] S --> D[Metadata discovery and composer suggestions] P[Submitted prompt and literal choices] --> A[Exact reference acceptance] S --> A A --> H[Unresolved names or typed failure: held task] A --> C[Accepted mode, revisions and record snapshot] C --> M[Bound field manifest or literal prompt projection] C --> B[Exact JSON inputs and pointer bindings] B --> X[Tool schema and ordinary authorization] X --> T[Tool execution] C --> U[Deferred idempotent usage accounting]

Binding-review flows explain how a successful recorded call becomes a user-approved rule for newly accepted tasks, including evidence, revision checks and the approval-generation boundary.

Correction-session and learned-workflow flows trace explicit Pause ownership, frozen Apply recovery, ordered teaching and fresh current-run dependencies.

Storage and authority

AgentParameterStore is both a factory and the standalone SQLite implementation. A supplied Controller hub or registered path owner selects MemoryParameterStore. That repository owns live values, audits and derived indexes; direct SQL access fails once RAM authority is selected. Disk recovery follows the shared checkpoint protocol. Standalone use retains schema version 2 and ordinary SQL transactions. Both representations contain plaintext values.

Canonical keys are normalized independently of display spelling. New reserved mention names are rejected; an existing conflicting entry can still be managed. get_exact uses canonical identity only. Legacy get can fall back to an alias substring, and legacy list search includes private values/context with SQL-style % and _ wildcards. Composer suggestion search uses literal metadata substrings and never searches stored values. A discovery match is not accepted authority.

Create/update validates recognized profiles before persistence. Unknown or untyped JSON remains ordinary data. RAM changes publish row, indexes and audit together; standalone mutations use their SQL transaction. Ordinary updates do not require a caller revision precondition. Auth token rotation instead uses compare_update_value, checking both creation and update timestamps for the target and every dependency in the same mutation transaction. A stale comparison returns no replacement. Usage increments leave configuration timestamps unchanged.

Updates and deletion invalidate known HTTP/Proxmox scopes and any attached Auth broker. RAM invalidation follows commit. Standalone update also invalidates after commit; its delete invalidates Auth before the SQL deletion and HTTP/Proxmox after commit. These external cache effects are not one atomic storage transaction.

The three directory defaults are seeded only when their canonical keys are absent. They contain Gateway environment references, not Controller paths. Reopening restores a deleted default; existing user edits are retained. The current three-default combination exceeds the default 4,000-character bound manifest budget; choose only needed references or configure a larger limit. This is a current admission limitation, not a failure to seed them.

Management and native entry points

Parameter routes expose explicit editor CRUD, audited raw reveal, metadata suggestions and model-assisted drafting. List statistics cover at most 1,000 rows. Detail responses include full Context JSON alongside the projected summary; reveal additionally returns complete Value JSON. The compatibility-named public_http_profile field contains a complete literal version-3 replacement, not a credential-free merge. Ordinary route edits do not require an expected revision.

The Parameters skill uses the same store and normal tool permissions. parameters.manage performs ordinary CRUD. parameters.patch instead requires an exact key and expected_updated_at, merges nested dictionaries while replacing other values, and preserves omitted fields. Both the patch and its merged value must fit 64 KiB. Changing profile_type is rejected. Typed validation and an atomic revision comparison precede persistence; successful patches invalidate connection/Auth caches. A conflict requires inspection and reconciliation rather than silently applying the edit to a newer record.

Native wrapper expansion advertises invoke_bound only for accepted bound parameters, and permits only already advertised capability tools or supported composites. It validates resolved schemas unconditionally, including each sequence/parallel/scheduled child, and compares routing/control identities before and after substitution. The dispatch copy contains exact inputs; the journal keeps the original symbolic call. Parameter reads separately test whole field pages against the projected conversation, current tools and model execution reservation. Oversized pages suggest half the requested entry limit; failure at one entry reports the capacity boundary without another smaller retry.

Acceptance, mode and restart

Reference acceptance uses the shared literal-aware mention parser: escaped references, inline/fenced code and reserved resource mentions do not become parameter candidates. Each remaining candidate resolves its exact canonical key; aliases and fuzzy retrieval never substitute another record. Unknown names remain unresolved so admission can hold the task. Explicit literal choices remain part of the accepted snapshot.

Version 3 snapshots capture bound or literal mode. The global binding setting defaults to off (literal mode) and is sampled for new acceptance. Version 2 retains literal behavior; unsupported historical bindings require resubmission. Existing accepted records are reused when resolving a continuation, rather than rereading edited values. Ordinary literal snapshots survive restart and deletion of the live record. Protected authentication profiles are an explicit exception described below.

The raw accepted expansion includes Value JSON, Context JSON, description, aliases, tags and the section header. It must fit the configured aggregate character limit before the bound field manifest is built. The manifest must also fit. The default is 4,000 characters through agent_parameter_prompt_max_chars / AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_PROMPT_MAX_CHARS. Paging field descriptions does not bypass the original full-value admission limit, and JSON is never silently truncated.

Admission can defer usage writes until task ownership is established. Actors named prompt_reference:<identity> deduplicate persisted usage events; ordinary usage calls do not share that idempotency rule. Returned convenience records increment their supplied count even on a deduplicated call, so callers needing authoritative counts reread the store. A usage-write failure is separate from resolution failure and may be reported after task acceptance. The task admission guide owns held-task retry and runtime-message behavior.

Exact inputs and model reads

Binding helpers read only the accepted snapshot. An empty source pointer selects the whole Value JSON. Other addresses use JSON Pointer escaping and a 1,024-character ceiling. The manifest contains absolute field addresses, types, revision and supplied metadata; its description wrappers are not part of the source pointer.

read_parameter supports projected values, recursive structure and field pages. Fields include containers in deterministic preorder, default to 16 entries and allow integer limits from 1 through 64. Only the fields view accepts pagination. The shared generator allocates whole entries fairly across selected records and supplies exact next-page actions. Overlong descendants are marked at their callable ancestor. Invalid pointers return at most eight bounded sibling suggestions plus a read action for the deepest valid ancestor; the runtime does not choose or execute a suggested field.

A bound invocation accepts 1–32 source/destination declarations. It copies arguments before applying them, requires destination parents to exist, fills absent object fields or existing null array slots, and rejects overlapping destinations. It cannot replace runtime routing/control metadata or the runtime-owned inputs.parameters namespace. Strings remain data; there is no interpolation or expression evaluation. The caller validates the resulting tool schema and applies ordinary authorization to the resolved values before execution.

Shell/Python preparation inserts the complete accepted namespace under inputs["parameters"]. A process-local marker prevents duplicate preparation. Operation provenance carries keys and accepted revisions rather than values or secret-derived hashes. Call previews replace runtime-supplied values with revision identities independently of optional redaction. This exact nested representation differs from legacy OF_PARAM_* scalar exports, which skip arrays/nulls and can collapse distinct paths to the same environment name.

Privacy and projections

Ordinary saved values and accepted checkpoints retain literal data. The sensitive flag is projection metadata, not encryption or a prohibition on tool use. PARAMETERS controls ordinary model/UI copies; AUDIT separately controls ordinary mutation audit copies. Historical names such as masked_value_json do not guarantee masking when the corresponding policy is off. Metadata and Context JSON are user-authored content and should not be mistaken for value-free secrets storage. See Redaction for policy ownership.

Auth privacy identifies protected account, OAuth, Email and selected secret profiles independently of optional redaction. Their accepted bindings contain permitted identity/revision projections; trusted provider code resolves private authority using its own lifecycle rules. They are also excluded from scalar shell export. Ordinary HTTP authentication types are not all in that protected set; OAuth/auth_ref HTTP profiles are. Use native HTTP tools for saved connections and their session/revision checks.

Legacy generic execution-value maps exclude all recognized typed profiles, while legacy shell export uses the narrower Auth-protected predicate. Those two helpers are not interchangeable privacy boundaries. Model value reads project the whole accepted tree before selecting a subtree so selecting /password does not discard its field provenance. None of these projections rewrites executor input.

Drafting, failures and verification

Draft extraction produces editable proposals only. With an enabled supplied client and store-related request, it tries structured model extraction; errors fall back to deterministic write-intent parsing. Fallback stages prefer whole JSON, pasted fields, connection details and then credential phrases. Confidence and missing-detail flags describe the draft, not successful persistence. Templates likewise return detached prefills without saving, connecting, granting capabilities or running inference.

Resolution diagnostics retain only allowlisted identities, counts and causes. Machine error codes distinguish storage busy, permission, full, corrupt and I/O failures. Historical free-form errors are never republished; exact known templates can recover safe facts, and unknown text yields a request to check again. Oversize notices show aggregate counts and at most five largest entries, without their values.

The package README maps every file. Binding contracts, field-page contracts, RAM storage checks and reference lifecycle tests exercise exact inputs, isolation, limits and recovery using temporary data and scripted models. They do not validate a live provider deployment.

Reviewed mapping authority

Parameter schema version 3 adds parameter_mapping_documents and immutable parameter_mapping_revisions. Both the RAM repository and standalone SQLite implement revision checks and idempotency. The shared checkpoint/export schema includes these tables; retention treats them as global Parameter Store configuration and audit history.

Correction sessions bind a request and run, then an invocation and its observed revision when selected. Opening a correction requests Pause; inspection alone never does. Preview resolves user-selected sources and validates corrected arguments without dispatch. Apply pins an accepted correction snapshot in native task state, journals the reviewed definition, commits an idempotent native amendment, and uses normal Resume. A partially completed application retains the same source snapshot, definition identity and amendment identity for recovery.

Canonical preparation resolves approved fields before schema validation, authorization and execution. Pending invocations retain proposed arguments, mapping revision, source revisions, resolved arguments and private environment data separately. Changes to saved sources cannot change already accepted inputs. Generic mappings match tool contract, workspace, Gateway, source identities and reviewed argument structure. SSH profiles match reviewed connection identity independently of remote-command text. Multiple candidates require selection; one explicit correction selection can be claimed by only one invocation.

The model receives bounded value-free mapping advice. An SSH profile has a symbolic hostname of the form smto-<mapping-id>.invalid; issuing the supplied literal SSH template explicitly selects that approved profile without transcribing credentials or source pointers. The runtime rechecks scope, enabled state, source identity/type and contract before materializing it. An unavailable symbolic profile produces an actionable error instead of being executed. Advice and ordinary model memory are not execution authority.

Prior-result sources carry the exact original operation, producer-argument digest and accepted producer workspace/Gateway scope. Within that task, resolution uses the owned receipt. Across tasks, a unique completed matching producer is required. Learned workflows additionally name the reviewed producer step and resolve only its fresh claimed receipt. No historical result value is copied into a definition.

/api/agent/parameter-corrections owns create/inspect/preview/apply/cancel. POST /api/agent/parameter-corrections/task starts or reopens a run-pinned call-selection session and requests cooperative Pause before selection. POST /{id}/select-call attaches an exact invocation with revision checks; the same session retains pause ownership through mapping and cancellation. Session inspection supports both selection and mapping phases, including after restart. Full and compact run snapshots expose only eligibility, call availability, and open-session metadata in parameter_correction; discovery never loads parameter values into those projections. Both UI clients mount the shared shortcut outside activity disclosure and retain stable controls during snapshot updates. /api/agent/parameter-mappings owns the library, immutable history and feedback. /api/agent/learned-workflows owns reviewed sequence capture and explicit runs, using the existing Agent-guided workflow execution guards. The saved-request Workflow API is unchanged. All mutations carry revisions and idempotency keys. parameters.changed notifications refresh shared clients after commits. Execution outcomes and user-confirmed correctness remain distinct; incorrect feedback records a revision suspension, including for pinned workflow references.

Validation includes mapping integration tests, desktop/mobile interaction, and a loopback SSH account implemented in the isolated fixture. The optional configured-model evaluation reports intended-target success and repeat-error rates separately from software test counts.

The local Ornith evaluation used one trial per phase. Binding without a learned mapping reached the intended target in 0/1 trials; its repeat-error rate was 1/1. After the reviewed correction, target success was 1/1 and repeat errors were 0/1. A new task using the same mapping for a different remote command also reached the intended target (1/1), with repeat errors 0/1. These measurements use a loopback-only SSH fixture and restricted command surface; they are not a general model reliability estimate. The correction phase starts from a deterministically seeded failed call.
